title: Alibi and Autopsy
premise: Ines Dravenmoor, the coroner of rain-soaked Hollowmere, is paid a retainer by a frightened stranger to prove a murder that hasn't happened yet — and within days, the predicted victim, councilwoman Mara Voss, turns up dead exactly as foretold. As Ines investigates, they discover the killer is someone with access to every autopsy report and case file: someone inside the town's small machinery of power, possibly the police captain Ellery Vane, the one person Ines has ever let close. The 'client' was the killer's first intended scapegoat, paying Ines in desperation. In the end, Ines must choose between the evidence that would clear their name and the man they love, staging a final autopsy reveal at the town hall that exposes Vane — who dies by his own hand rather than surrender the belonging he killed to keep.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former rural paramedic who spent a decade answering calls in towns too small for their own morgue. They write mysteries about the quiet rot beneath picturesque places, drawing on the strange intimacy of knowing everyone's secrets before they're confessed.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Ines Dravenmoor's POV. A hooded stranger leaves an envelope of cash on the mortuary slab with a single instruction: prove that Mara Voss will not be murdered on the solstice. Ines, who has never refused a fee or lost a case, takes it half as curiosity, half as insult. The beat is wary intrigue — a professional's pride pricked by an impossible contract.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with flashbacks to their arrival in Hollowmere years ago. They canvass the town they know bone-deep, learning Mara Voss has been receiving threats over her plan to sell the old mill lands. Captain Ellery Vane — Ines's quiet, unspoken love — dismisses the warnings. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with duty, as Ines realizes asking Vane for help means handing him the case.

chapters.title: Solstice
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The night of the solstice arrives; Ines stakes out Voss's house through freezing rain and still finds her dead at dawn, posed precisely as the letter described. The medical details are flawless — too flawless, matching techniques only someone who reads autopsy reports would know. Beat: cold horror and professional humiliation; Ines has failed their first contract.

chapters.title: The Client Vanishes
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The stranger who hired them cannot be found — until Ines traces the retainer's cash to Daniel Okafor, a mill-lands surveyor whose fingerprints are suddenly all over the crime scene. Okafor swears he was framed and begs Ines to find the truth. Beat: dread deepening into resolve; Ines realizes the client wasn't predicting the murder but fleeing it.

chapters.title: Case File Ghost
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, alternating with brief police-procedural sections from Deputy Sorrel Ndiaye. Someone has been accessing archived reports digitally — including Ines's own autopsies going back a decade. Only three people have clearance: Ines, the records clerk, and Captain Vane. Beat: creeping paranoia; the investigation turns inward toward the people Ines trusts.

chapters.title: What the Body Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A second death: the records clerk, drowned in her own bathtub, staged as suicide — again with details lifted from an old case file Ines wrote. Grief-stricken and now a suspect themselves, Ines hides evidence from Vane for the first time in their career. Beat: guilt and self-betrayal; love against duty begins to cut both ways.

chapters.title: The Long Confession
chapters.summary: Ines and Vane share whiskey and half-truths in the mortuary after hours. Vane reveals Voss was about to expose department corruption tied to the mill sale — and that he'd been investigating it alone. Ines nearly tells him everything, then notices his boots match prints from the solstice scene. Beat: heartbreak suspended; the reader feels the trap closing around them both.

chapters.title: Autopsy of a Town
chapters.summary: Ines's POV with interludes from Okafor in hiding. Digging into Voss's sealed documents, Ines reconstructs the motive: Vane built his whole identity on being Hollowmere's protector, and Voss's revelations would have made him its corrupter. He killed to preserve his belonging. Beat: terrible clarity — Ines understands the killer completely, which means understanding the man they love.

chapters.title: The Trap at Town Hall
chapters.summary: Ines stages a public 'preliminary autopsy' at the town hall meeting, announcing evidence that implicates Okafor — bait only the true killer could not resist correcting. Vane steps forward to contradict the timeline with a detail never released, in front of the whole town and Deputy Ndiaye's recorder. Beat: high-wire climax; Ines sacrifices their reputation to spring the trap.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cornered, Vane confesses privately to Ines alone — a last, awful intimacy — then takes his life before arrest, leaving Ines his own case file: a full confession naming Okafor innocent. Weeks later, Ines buries him in the cemetery where they know every grave by name, and finally closes the case they were paid to prevent. Beat: mourning, absolution, and hard-won belonging on new terms.
